Umuyobozi Mukuru wa Banki ya Kigali (BK), Dr. Diane Karusisi, yatangaje ko iyi banki yiyemeje gukomeza gufasha abashoramari n’abacuruzi bahuye n’ingaruka z’inkongi y’umuriro yibasiye isoko rya GOICO riherereye mu Karere ka Musanze, kugira ngo bongere kubaka ibikorwa byabo by’ubucuruzi.

Ibi yabigarutseho ubwo yari mu ruzinduko rw’akazi mu Karere ka Musanze, aho yasuye ishami rya BK, aganira n’abakozi baryo ndetse anasura abakiriya ba banki bakorera mu nzego zitandukanye, barimo ibigo by’amashuri, uruganda rwa A1 Iron & Steel Rwanda n’abashoramari n’abacururizaga muri GOICO.

Mu bigo by’uburezi yasuye harimo Virunga Valley Academy, INES Ruhengeri na Excel International Academy, aho baganiriye ku mikoranire yabo na BK ndetse n’imishinga bafite bifuza ko iyi banki yabunganiramo.

Muri INES Ruhengeri, Umuyobozi w’ikigo, Fr. Dr. Jean Bosco Baribeshya, yashimye imikoranire bafitanye na BK, avuga ko iyi banki yabafashije mu bikorwa bitandukanye birimo no kubona inguzanyo zo kwagura ibikorwa by’ishuri.

Birumvikana ko ari ho tunyuza amafaranga dukoresha, ariko iranadufasha mu kuduha inguzanyo iyo dushaka kwagura ibikorwa byacu, bigatuma turushaho gutera imbere.”

Yakomeje avuga ko bifuza ko BK yabafasha mu mishinga itandukanye, irimo inyubako iri kubakwa muri iki gihe, ndetse ko bafite n’indi mishinga bifuza gufatanyamo na yo.

Yavuze ko kuba BK ifata umwanya wo gusura abakiriya bayo, ikaganira na bo ku byo bakeneye, bibashimisha kuko bituma bakorana baziranye kandi bahuje icyerekezo cy’iterambere.

Abubatse GOICO basabye koroherezwa kwishyura inguzanyo

Nyuma yo gusura ibigo by’uburezi n’uruganda rwa A1 Iron & Steel Rwanda, Dr. Karusisi yanasuye abashoramari bagize uruhare mu kubaka isoko rya GOICO ndetse n’abacururizagamo, kugira ngo yumve ibibazo bahuye na byo nyuma y’inkongi y’umuriro yaryibasiye.

Aba bacuruzi n’abashoramari basobanuriye ubuyobozi bwa BK ingaruka z’iyi nkongi, banagaragaza ubufasha bakeneye kugira ngo bongere kwiyubaka.

Umuyobozi w’Urugaga rw’Abikorera mu Ntara y’Amajyaruguru, Tugengwenayo Theonase, yavuze ko BK yababaye hafi kuva batangira umushinga wo kubaka isoko rya GOICO, ibaha inguzanyo ndetse ikomeza kubaba hafi mu bihe by’imbogamizi.

Yagize ati “Muri kiriya gikorwa cy’ishoramari ryo kubaka isoko rya GOICO ryahiye, BK yaduhaye inguzanyo mu ntangiriro zo kuryubaka, ndetse no hagati aho twagiye tugira ibibazo, ikomeza kutuba hafi.”

Yasobanuye ko nyuma y’inkongi hari inguzanyo zigera kuri miliyari y’amafaranga y’u Rwanda zari zitarishyurwa, bityo asaba BK kubafasha mu korohereza abashoramari kwishyura, by’umwihariko bahagarika inyungu kuri izo nguzanyo mu gihe bagihangana n’ingaruka z’icyo cyago.

Guverineri w’Intara y’Amajyaruguru, Mugabowagahunde Maurice, yashimiye BK kuba ikomeje kwegera abahuye n’ingaruka z’inkongi yibasiye isoko rya GOICO, avuga ko ibiganiro bagiranye bigamije gushaka ibisubizo byafasha abacuruzi n’abashoramari kongera ibikorwa byabo.

Yakomeje avuga ko bifuzaga kumvikana ku buryo abacuruzi n’abanyiri inyubako boroherezwa kwishyura inguzanyo, ndetse n’abandi bagahabwa ubufasha bwo kongera kuzahura ibikorwa byabo by’ubucuruzi.

Igikurikiyeho ni ugushyiraho uburyo ku ishami rya BK, kugira ngo buri wese azajye ahagera bakumva ikibazo cye, bityo ubufasha butangirire aho.”

Yashimye kandi umuco wa BK wo kwegera abakiriya no kumva ibyifuzo byabo, asaba n’andi mabanki kuwugiraho.

BK yiyemeje gukomeza gushyigikira abashoramari

Yagize ati “Uyu munsi twaje i Musanze, aho abakiriya bacu benshi bagize ibyago, barimo abubatse GOICO n’abayikoreragamo, kugira ngo tuganire dufate ingamba zo kongera kubaka, ariko no kuzahura ubucuruzi bwo muri Musanze muri rusange.

Abo dusura ni abakiriya bacu. Turabashimira gukorana natwe, bakaduha ibikorwa byabo, natwe tukumva imihigo n’ingamba bafite kugira ngo tubafashe kubishyira mu bikorwa. Akazi kacu ni ugushyigikira ubucuruzi kugira ngo ba nyirabwo babashe kugera ku nzozi zabo.”

Ku bijyanye na INES Ruhengeri, Dr. Karusisi yavuze ko ari kimwe mu bigo bamaze igihe bakorana na cyo, kandi ko cyabagaragarije imishinga gifite kigamije guteza imbere ireme ry’uburezi.

Yavuze ko muri iyo mishinga harimo kubaka ahazajya hakorerwa amahugurwa ngiro y’abanyeshuri (workshops), Digital Hub ndetse n’ibindi bikorwa remezo byafasha ikigo kwagura ubushobozi bwacyo.

Ati “INES Ruhengeri ni ishuri rikomeye tumaze igihe dukorana na ryo. Batweretse ingamba bafite, inyubako bafite, aho bashaka kubaka Digital Hub n’ahantu bashaka kubaka workshops z’abanyeshuri kugira ngo bazamure ireme ry’uburezi. Batweretse aho bageze n’aho bashaka ko BK iza kubunganira kugira ngo barangize izo nyubako.”

Dr. Karusisi yavuze ko mu myaka isaga 60 BK imaze ikorera mu Rwanda, ikomeje gushyira imbaraga mu kwegera abakiriya bayo, kumva imishinga yabo no gufatanya na bo mu kuyishyira mu bikorwa.

Yasobanuye ko gushyigikira ubucuruzi n’ishoramari bifite uruhare mu guteza imbere ubukungu bw’igihugu, binyuze mu guhanga imirimo, kongera umusaruro no gutanga imisoro.

Uru ruzinduko rwa Dr. Diane Karusisi mu Karere ka Musanze ni kimwe mu bikorwa bigamije gukomeza umubano wa BK n’abakiriya bayo, kumenya ibyo bakeneye no gushaka ibisubizo byafasha ibikorwa byabo gukomeza gutera imbere.

MN202611_apriulo64r.t: Industrial output increased by 7.2 per cent in September 2026 compared with the same month last year, driven largely by growth in electricity generation and mining activities, according to the latest figures from the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR). The growth was higher than the annual average increase of 5.6 per cent recorded during the period, reflecting improved performance across most industrial activities. ALSO READ: Industrial output grows 6.8% in August Electricity output registered the strongest annual growth, rising by 15.5 per cent, followed by mining and quarrying, which increased by 12 per cent. Water and waste management output grew by 11.5 per cent, while manufacturing recorded a modest increase of 0.4 per cent. Despite recording a lower growth rate than mining, electricity made the largest contribution to the overall increase in industrial output, accounting for three percentage points. Manufacturing contributed 2.4 percentage points, while mining and quarrying added 1.6 percentage points. ALSO READ: Industrial output rises 6.6 per cent in July Manufacturing records modest growth Manufacturing, which accounts for 68.1 per cent of the industrial production index, registered a 0.4 per cent annual increase. The performance was supported by food processing, which grew by 1.7 per cent, beverage and tobacco manufacturing, which increased by 4.8 per cent, and metal products, machinery and equipment, which recorded a 6.1 per cent rise. ALSO READ: June industrial output climbs 6.2% on manufacturing growth Other manufacturing activities also registered annual growth, including wood, paper and printing (3.3 per cent), chemicals, rubber and plastic products (3.4 per cent), and furniture and other manufacturing (4.6 per cent). However, manufacturing output declined by 8.1 per cent compared with August 2026, indicating a slowdown on a monthly basis. Mining and quarrying output increased by 9.2 per cent compared with August, while electricity output declined by 4.4 per cent over the same period. Industrial output edges up monthly Overall industrial production increased by 0.9 per cent between August and September. The increase came despite monthly declines in manufacturing and electricity, with mining and quarrying recording strong recovery and water and waste management output remaining almost unchanged, declining by 0.1 per cent. NISR's industrial production index tracks monthly output among businesses operating in the formal sector, defined as those registered with tax authorities. The index covers mining and quarrying, manufacturing, electricity, and water and waste management. It excludes construction activities because of data limitations.

Passengers on this Aer Lingus flight to Rome were diverted to a military base in France after a bomb threat

The "Male State", an extremist misogynistic group named in this week's hoax bomb threats to Italian airports, has denied any link to the false warnings causing flight disruption across Europe .

The comments to the BBC came as reports of more bomb scares to airlines began appearing, including on a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon and a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome which was diverted to Venice.

Bomb threats were also reported to a number of high-profile Irish media organisations on Friday, prompting evacuations and a statement from the Irish government suggesting a "co-ordinated campaign of disruption".

Replying to the BBC Russian Service, an account on Telegram - one of several linked to the so-called "Male State" and its founder Vladislav Pozdnyakov - mocked any suggestion the group was involved in emailing the threats.

"What Male State? Where have you seen it? It hasn't existed for many years," the message on the channel reads. "If tomorrow they sign a [threat] letter, say, from Putin, will you then try to reach our president to ask your stupid question?"

The message claimed that "fighters" of the "Male State" had planted explosives on two incoming flights

The group was banned in Russia in 2021 and Pozdnyakov is now thought to live abroad. It has since renamed itself in some places as "Male Legion".

The initial hoax email, seen by the BBC, was sent on Thursday at 07:21 with the subject title: warning of a threat.

It was addressed to several offices and individuals at Aeroporti di Roma (ADR), the airport managing company in Rome, as well as accounts at the city's Fiumicino airport itself. The originating email address seems to be linked to the state health services in Bogota, Colombia.

It's not clear whether other countries' airports or airlines received the same or similar threat. At least one warning made on Friday appears to have come by phone, not email.

Written in word perfect Italian, the bizarre text sent to Rome on Thursday claimed that "fighters" of the "Male State" had planted explosives on two incoming flights in an attack on Italy's "feminist regime" that would be "remembered forever".

One flight was diverted as a result - ordered to land in France – another was escorted into Rome by Italian air force jets, scrambled for the second time this week. No explosives were found on either plane, or any other that reported receiving bomb threats.

Asked why this particular email was taken so seriously, a source at ADR in Rome told the BBC that such warnings were extremely unusual. They didn't remember anything similar in recent years.

Despite the Russian group's denial, Italy's La Stampa newspaper appears in no doubt that "Male State" was behind the threats, asking in an article whether it is acting as "the regime's armed wing".

"Attacking, and being able to deny the attacks...is part of the Russian game plan," the paper writes , external .

One Telegram channel linked to Pozdnyakov is mainly filled with virulently pro-Russian messaging about the war on Ukraine and other posts highlighting problems and tensions in Europe, including recent youth protests.

The online investigation team at Bellingcat, who studied the group back in 2022, called it then a "vocal and vile online booster" of the Russian invasion, with a clear extremist far-right ideology.

As the Europe-wide hunt continues for who is behind the spate of hoax mails, and whether they are being co-ordinated - or could be the work of copycats - Italy's defence minister has warned of a "strategy to increase chaos".

Guido Crosetto noted that he had been talking of the "hybrid threat" to Europe for some years.

"It seems to me that, day after day, from incidents involving refrigerators to the blood supply in France and now these false alarms, there are those who have an interest in fuelling tensions," the minister said on Thursday, referring to a spate of recent cyber attacks that boosted supermarket fridge temperatures, destroying mountains of produce.

"Our interest is to do the opposite and ensure the country's security," Crosetto said.

The spaceport site is on the A' Mhoine Peninsula in Sutherland

A rockets manufacturer says the mothballed Sutherland Spaceport could become its first launch site outside the US.

Colorado-based Leap has agreed to work with Highlands and Islands Enterprise (HIE), which owns the area of peatland near Tongue, to develop the plans.

Little work has been done at the site after Moray-headquartered rockets firm Orbex put construction on hold in 2024 . The company later collapsed and its assets were sold off .

Leap said the spaceport could potentially be used for launching small satellites for customers in the UK and mainland Europe.

More stories from the Highlands and Islands

News from the Highlands and Islands on BBC Sounds

Leap is designing rockets that could be mass produced in factories.

Chief executive Chris Beckman said: "We're not just building a rocket. We're building a global logistics network, and a network needs launch sites wherever customers require them.

"Sutherland is an ideal starting point for a network that begins in Europe, and HIE shares our ambition to make recurring spaceflight from Scotland real."

HIE and Economy Secretary Stephen Flynn have welcomed the agreement.

The site is on Melness Crofters Estate, an area of small-scale farms on the A' Mhoine Peninsula in Sutherland in the north-west Highlands.

Chairwoman Dorothy Pritchard said the estate was delighted to welcome Leap as a potential launch operator.

She said: "We believe their presence here will be an important step towards establishing a thriving and sustainable spaceport that can bring long-term benefits to Sutherland and the UK's growing space industry.

"Alongside other UK launch sites, both developed and emerging, an operational Sutherland Spaceport will become an integral part of a resilient and diverse UK launch ecosystem, securing the UK position within the global space economy, something we welcome and support.

"Melness Crofters Estate looks forward to seeing the spaceport become a driver of economic opportunity."

Last month, the UK and German governments said they planned to use another Scottish spaceport - SaxaVord in Shetland - as part of increased co-operation between the two countries.

The agreement followed a meeting between Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin last week.

In a joint statement, the two governments said they would deepen strategic co-operation on civil, commercial, security and defence interests in space.

SaxaVord in Unst is the UK's first fully-licensed spaceport and has regulatory approval for up to 30 rocket launches a year.

The Official UK Rap Chart will be presented by DJ Kenny Allstar

British rap artists will step into the spotlight later when BBC Radio 1Xtra launches the first ever dedicated rap chart based on UK listening figures.

DJ Kenny Allstar, who'll host the countdown on Friday nights, has one word: "Finally".

"If we have our own fair playing field where we can all be celebrated... it then feels fair and it feels exciting," he tells BBC Newsbeat.

Currently artists compete across genres for a spot in the Official Singles Chart, but Allstar says this is dominated by pop music, making it harder for other genres to be heard.

Perhaps with the exception of heavyweights like Central Cee and Dave, who broke chart records with Sprinter back in 2023 , "it's not easy for any artist to go against Sabrina Carpenter and Taylor Swift every week," he says.

Compiled by the Official Charts Company, 20 rap singles from British artists will be ranked each week based on streams and sales in the UK.

It follows the launch of other genre-specific charts including for R&B, 'homegrown' albums and British Asian music.

Allstar hopes it'll give UK rap a boost as he acknowledges it has taken a bit of a beating recently with prominent artists like Skepta and Digga saying the quality of music coming from the scene has dipped.

"Future broadcasters and talent will benefit from this forever, I'm super gassed."

Allstar has long been a champion of UK rap and currently presents the Rap Show on BBC Radio 1, which he describes as "the show I always wanted as a kid".

This new role is "a pinch me moment," he says.

The Official Charts Company previously listed the 40 top selling R&B and hip hop tracks on its website, but there had been nowhere for fans to listen to the chart.

"It was literally just a bunch of numbers and text, so it kind of existed but not in this capacity," Allstar says.

Each week will likely see at least three or four new artists in the chart, giving emerging talent a chance to be heard by hundreds of thousands of listeners.

"What we can finally have is UK rap having its dedicated space where artists can just be celebrated," he says.

Eric Hunter, from the Official Charts Company, says the countdown will be "an amazing opportunity to shine a light on more artists, document the culture and give emerging talent a way to track their progress alongside their peers".

The company says UK rap is "one of the country's most influential and fast-moving music scenes" and the chart will celebrate both established names and the next generation of rappers driving the scene.

The debut show coincides with Skepta's long-awaited sixth studio album and Allstar says he expects to see the rapper feature in the chart.

"It's looking promising, but the only way you can find out is if you listen in," he says.

The Official UK Rap Chart will broadcast on 1Xtra each Friday from 22:00-23:00 and will be available after on BBC Sounds.

KIGALI – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is threatening to withdraw from the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF) if Rwandan incumbent Louise Mushikiwabo secures a third term as Secretary-General, adding a new diplomatic dimension to the contest ahead of the organisation’s summit in Cambodia.

The reported threat comes as Kinshasa steps up efforts to prevent Mushikiwabo’s re-election and promote its own candidate, Juliana Amato Lumumba, daughter of Congo’s independence leader and first Prime Minister, Patrice Emery Lumumba.

Mushikiwabo, who has led the organisation since January 2019, is seeking another four-year mandate. Rwanda has officially endorsed her candidacy, citing her record in leading institutional reforms and strengthening the organisation.

According to reports published on November 6, Congolese authorities are considering withdrawing their country from the organisation if the Rwandan candidate is re-elected.

The threat was reported by Jeune Afrique and subsequently carried by Congolese media. However, there has been no publicly available formal announcement confirming that Kinshasa has made a decision to leave the organisation.

The development comes amid strained relations between Kigali and Kinshasa over the conflict in eastern Congo, with the Congolese government accusing Rwanda of supporting the M23/AFC armed group, an allegation Rwanda denies.

Rwanda has consistently raised concerns about threats posed by armed groups operating in eastern Congo, particularly the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR).

Throughout her re-election campaign, Mushikiwabo has highlighted the changes and reforms achieved during her tenure, arguing that her record demonstrates the organisation’s progress under her leadership.

She has also gained considerable international visibility, with several member states hosting her as she seeks support for a third term. Her supporters say she has raised the profile of the Francophonie, strengthened its international engagement and made the organisation more visible on the global stage.

By contrast, Kinshasa’s campaign against her re-election appears increasingly centred on her Rwandan nationality and the diplomatic tensions between the two countries, rather than specific shortcomings in her management or performance at the organisation. The DRC has yet to publicly present a substantive case against her record as Secretary-General.

The diplomatic tensions have increasingly spilled into the Francophonie leadership contest, with Kinshasa questioning Mushikiwabo’s leadership while Kigali maintains that her performance and experience should be the basis for determining the next Secretary-General.

Russell Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault

Warning: This article contains graphic descriptions of sexual acts

No British celebrity navigated the cultural changes of the early 21st Century better than Russell Brand.

His life has been one long personal rebrand.

He morphed from provocative stand-up comic to TV star and Hollywood actor. He became a YouTuber and political activist, taking up left-wing causes around issues of inequality in the 2010s, then Covid conspiracies and in 2024 supporting Donald Trump for president. That same year he was baptised as a Christian in London's River Thames.

Now he has a new persona to try on: convicted rapist.

On Thursday, the disgraced comedian was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault at Southwark Crown Court , following a three-week trial.

As he faces jail, it's clear that the behaviour that formed the backdrop to Brand's prosecution is the same behaviour that helped elevate him in the first place.

Brand performing at the MTV Video Music Awards a year after his memoir was published

Brand shot to fame as a sexually outrageous libertine whose risque humour thrilled audiences.

He cultivated the image of an insatiable, shameless womaniser. Sex, drugs and excess were central to his comic material.

Over the decade of his offending, Brand sold out stand-up comedy venues and theatres, broadcasters - including MTV, Channel 4 and the BBC - started to throw money at him.

With his backcombed hair and drainpipe black jeans, Brand regaled audiences at his stand-up comedy gigs with the graphic details of his sexual exploits: anal sex, prostitutes and orgies.

He simulated masturbation and sex on stage. He said he liked oral sex with women "where it goes in their neck a little bit" and their "mascara runs a little bit," acting it out on stage.

Even Brand's own barrister called the humour "a product of its time," reminding the jury in the trial that this graphic sexualised comedy was viewed as "radical and different" back then.

Barely a generation later, many will view it as deeply rooted misogyny dressed up as humour. But these were different times.

Back then lads' magazines ruled - with their covers and double page spreads full of topless glamour models and half-naked female celebrities

The late nineties and early noughties in Britain were an era that celebrated casual sexism and often elevated celebrities who espoused it.

In 1999, FHM projected a naked photo of the Scottish TV presenter Gail Porter on to the Houses of Parliament. She only found out when she saw it on the news, and spoke later about how it deeply affected her mental health.

What might now be termed toxic masculinity was often deemed funny, seen by some as good old-fashioned male humour. By others it was viewed as palatable because they believed it was being done with an apparently ironic eyebrow raise.

"There is no question he was a very talented stand-up," says Sarah Ditum, author of Toxic: Women, Fame and the Noughties. "There was an appetite for taboo breaking.

"I think it looks very old hat if you look back on that stuff. It's dated horribly and I don't think many people are going to be keen to defend Brand's act now knowing that it reflected his real world behaviour rather than an ironic performance."

My Booky Wook topped the Sunday Times bestseller chart for seven weeks in 2007

But there were clues at the time that his outrageous stage act did not stop when the show ended - most publicly in his 2007 bestselling memoir, My Booky Wook.

"I'm a bloke from Grays with a good job and a terrific haircut who's been given a Wonka ticket to a lovely sex factory 'cos of ol' fame."

Of course, many of his sexual partners consented. As his defence barrister told the jury "he devoted himself for many years to a highly promiscuous life", reminding them that "having lots of sex is completely lawful".

My Booky Wook, which topped the Sunday Times bestseller chart for seven weeks in 2007 and sold 600,000 copies in hardback in the UK, opens with him checking into a clinic for sex addiction. He writes about going to lap dancing clubs and having "a lot" of oral sex in toilets and many threesomes.

"The rules change when you're famous. In that case two is often better than either none or one."

He writes about how an MTV PR "reminded me that I put lap dances and prostitutes on her gold card and got the hotel to give me cash on her account without her prior knowledge".

The Observer called it "a scandalous, libidinous memoir that is better written and more entertaining than any number of celebrity autobiographies that clog the shelves".

Heat said: "You come away from the book feeling like you really know - and like - the real Russell."

You can't imagine a celebrity these days writing a memoir in which he claims that at stage school a primetime actress, whom he names, "kissed me once in a corridor" and for years afterwards he'd tell people "'I had sex with her… And by sex, I mean bumming'".

But it's all told in a jokey, revelatory way, by "a bloke from Essex who likes birds with big bottoms and big boobs…. Lovely dolly-birds".

Meeting crowds backstage in Sydney in 2010

In light of his offending, writing that was celebrated for being frank, honest - and very funny - now looks anything but.

People "are willing to mistake irony and self-awareness for truth telling and trustworthiness," says Ditum. "The idea that he made these jokes about being this kind of sexual monster was supposed to convince you that he wasn't actually a sexual monster in real life."

Did normalising his behaviour allow him to hide in plain sight? Were the media companies who embraced him, the comedy venues who promoted him, the audiences who laughed at his humour, in some way complicit?

A former TV boss who didn't want to be named explained the thinking of his peers like this: "You've got this charismatic presenter who appears to be very, very good and you don't want to lose that.

"The women who were being persecuted didn't feel empowered to speak up and the few who did feel empowered might have been classed as troublemakers but certainly weren't really listened to because you didn't want to lose the star. That was the process."

Indeed, in Brand's trial, one of the complainants told the court she didn't report what had happened to her because she didn't think she would be believed in "those laddish culture times".

"It was my word against his," she said in her evidence.

Jo Caulfield, a contemporary of Brand's on the early noughties stand-up circuit, says she initially found him "utterly charming" but she sees that he was "enabled and nobody will say anything against it".

"People have people around them, promoters, assistants in TV. It's in the hierarchy of TV. If a runner [an entry-level production assistant] goes to his dressing room and he gets his knob out, it's like, 'oh, come on, don't make a fuss.'"

And while safeguarding standards have been heavily tightened in some parts of the entertainment world, she says it "still goes on".

"Nobody wants to upset the star. This person is making them money so everybody down the food chain better not say anything if they behave badly," says Caulfield.

At the end of My Booky Wook, Brand writes "I have done some terrible things over the course of this booky wook… I mean, over my life."

Elliot Anderson started his career at Newcastle before moves to Nottingham Forest and Manchester City

Elliot Anderson's stock has risen astronomically and there were considerable expectations on the midfielder's shoulders after sealing a £116m move from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City in the summer.

The 24-year-old established himself as one of the best players in the Premier League and has become a key man for England, helping Thomas Tuchel's side to a third-placed finish at this summer's World Cup.

His highly impressive performances for Forest over the past two seasons had him tracked by the likes of Manchester United and Arsenal before his move to Etihad Stadium.

European football expert Guillem Balague said on BBC Match of the Day he had spoken to City manager Enzo Maresca in the summer and asked if he wants to sign Bournemouth 's Alex Scott and Crystal Palace 's Adam Wharton.

The Italian's response was "no", adding: "Anderson is going to become the key player for England, not just City."

Anderson may well be afforded a generous reception when he makes his return to the City Ground on Saturday, with Forest supporter Ellie Molloson telling BBC Sport: "I know the stadium will be ringing with 'Geordie Maradona'.

"It will be bittersweet because we miss him, but we are quite proud of just how fantastic a player he is."

Few Forest fans will "begrudge him for his whopping move", but is Anderson managing to live up to the hype in the early days of his City career?

Anderson was one of the standout central midfielders in the Premier League last season.

He topped the rankings for a number of metrics such as touches of the ball, winning possession, contesting duels and drawing the most fouls.

His influence was striking despite featuring in a struggling Forest side which had four different managers and finished only five points above the relegation zone.

The former Newcastle player's tireless work-rate means he has effectively replaced Bernardo Silva and Rodri at City, making the step up to a side that won two trophies last season and could challenge for the title again.

Though Anderson has not fully replicated the outright league-leading dominance he showcased across several metrics last season, his underlying numbers remain elite.

He has drawn more fouls (28) than any other player in the division, while he ranks second for duels won (66) and third for successful passes (610) and touches on the ball (851).

Only Tottenham 's Jan Paul van Hecke and Arsenal 's Declan Rice have managed more successful passes in the opposition half and line-breaking passes than Anderson, but the City midfielder has played at least 66 minutes fewer than both.

Anderson's deep-lying number six role means he has only one goal and two assists in 14 games this season, though he did lay on Erling Haaland's winner against RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.

"He has been amazing," said Haaland afterwards. "He has had an amazing start to his City career and that is what you expect. You have to come straight in and perform.

"It is not easy to come in, you need to adapt and new players and a new coach, so he he has been impressive. Respect."

Elliot Anderson a 'potential legend' at Man City

In Tuesday's training session open to the media before City's trip to Leipzig, some players came out looking relaxed in groups but Anderson emerged by himself, doing kick-ups with a laser focus on the ball.

It perhaps hints at a steely determination to remain fixated and give his best at every opportunity, whether that be in training or during the intensity of a match.

Anderson was the first to step up in one of the group drills and was deemed the winner during a set-up which involved a slalom with the ball before smashing a finish into a mini net.

Asked if he was surprised at how quickly Anderson had settled in to life at City, Maresca told BBC Sport: "Knowing him now, he is a guy who wants to learn every day and we sat with him with video [analysis].

"He wants to understand things, he wants to learn and improve and for a manager it's a dream because you know that he wants to learn and you can do different things."

Molloson adds: "The way Anderson reads the game, the way he dominates midfield, he is such an intelligent football player and he is so young, there is still so much more to come from him.

"He is a leader on the pitch and I just think he is phenomenal. I think Forest fans would definitely have him back in a heartbeat."

Maresca has acknowledged Anderson's box-to-box qualities but sees him as City's number six this season. The demands of this role differ from how Anderson has previously been used.

Following Manchester City 's 4–1 win over Crystal Palace in August, Anderson said: "I'm loving [my role but] it's a bit different to what I've been used to. I've got to be a bit more structured, that's what I'm learning, to stay in my position. At Forest I was doing a little bit more."

His physicality, intensity and intelligence make him an excellent front-footed midfielder, capable of pressing players high or wide, winning the ball and starting attacks. When City have pressed man-to-man but been played through, Anderson has often impressively stopped attacks alone.

Brighton launch a dangerous counter-attack but Anderson impressively wins the ball back

Anderson's value in a more expansive role was seen in his assist for Haaland's winner at Leipzig this week, as he drove with the ball before playing a cross, reminiscent of Kevin de Bruyne.

Although City's holding midfielder, Anderson's skillset makes him effective across the pitch

The same qualities that Anderson posesses have also been exploited at times.

Habitually, he reacts to players more than thinking about positions, as he is able to win the ball back more often than not from most players. As a result, some opponents have looked to position themselves near him before moving away, enticing the Englishman to follow.

Sunderland 's Enzo le Fee made constant off-the-ball runs around and beyond Anderson in September . The England midefielder, almost magnetically, locked on to Le Fee, tracking those runs, which left space in front of City's defence.

Paris St-Germain and Brighton also used these decoy runs to pull Anderson away, creating space in midfield.

Here is an example of Le Fee using Anderson's front-footedness against him. By dropping deep and wide, Le Fee entices Anderson to follow him, vacating his holding midfield position

This opens up space in the centre of the pitch for Sunderland to find their striker, Brian Brobbey, in one pass

Ayyoub Bouaddi has been trialled alongside Anderson in midfield. When Anderson does vacate the holding midfield position to press, something we saw against PSG, a second defensive midfielder alongside him can help protect the centre of the pitch – a temporary fix as Anderson moulds his impressive skillset to Maresca's asks.

In 2021, Guardiola reflected on Rodri's first season, saying: "Last season he moved too much. The holding midfielder has to be there, don't move, be there." In 2024, he won the Ballon d'Or.

City will certainly be pleased with the quality of Anderson so far. It would also be fair to say his debut season has begun better than Rodri's did in 2020. But both City and Anderson will be hoping for a development in positional understanding that mimics the player he was brought in to replace.

Thomas Tuchel has named three uncapped players in his England squad

England manager Thomas Tuchel said Cole Palmer "misses too many chances to impress" after not selecting the Chelsea forward for November's Nations League fixtures.

Palmer, 24, dropped out of England's squad for their previous games in early autumn and is absent again for matches against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November and Spain in Madrid on Sunday, 15 November.

Tuchel has instead handed Fulham's Josh King and Borussia Dortmund's Jobe Bellingham their first England call-ups. Both players are attacking midfielders.

"We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together," said Tuchel.

"We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He is kind of an extra player and he can play all four positions.

"I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

"We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress."

Jobe, 21, joins his brother Jude in the England squad - and they could be the first pair of siblings to feature in an England line-up since Gary and Phil Neville.

England sit second behind Spain in group A3 of the Nations League with three wins and a loss.

One more point from their remaining two matches will secure a place in the two-legged quarter-finals in March, with the winners of those ties advancing to the Nations League Finals in June.

'Palmer misses too many opportunities to impress' - Tuchel

Catch-up with all Thomas Tuchel's responses at his squad selection news conference

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton & Hove Albion), James Trafford (Leeds United)

Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Marc Guehi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Jarell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)

Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), James Garner (Everton), Josh King (Fulham), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea)

The selection of Jobe Bellingham for the senior squad means he continues to follow in the footsteps of his older brother.

Both graduates of the Birmingham City academy, the brothers were regular selections in England youth line-ups.

Jobe joined Dortmund from Sunderland in summer 2025 in a deal worth up to £31m, having helped the Wearside club win promotion to the Premier League via the play-offs.

The move mirrored one made by Jude, 23, who played for the German side between 2020 and 2023 before signing for Real Madrid.

Tuchel said England Under-21 coach Lee Carsley had been "speaking very highly" of Jobe Bellingham "for a while".

"He is the captain of the under-21s so I think the door should always be open and the pathway should always be open for special performances over a long period of time and that is what Jobe has done," he added.

"He found his way and his rhythm with Dortmund, where he has had an excellent start to the season. He is a regular starter there and now very influential."

Bellingham has been preferred to Kobbie Mainoo, with Tuchel saying the Manchester United midfielder, who was an early withdrawal from the last squad, has had a "difficult spell with his club".

"The door is always open for younger players to overtake and make their mark," he added.

King has had a strong start to the Premier League season, scoring two goals and making one assist, and has played at every youth level for England.

The 19-year-old Fulham academy graduate has scored one goal in nine appearances for England Under-21s, and Tuchel called him "a fantastic character" who "gives us a bit of flexibility".

"We decided to nominate 22 outfield players for flexibility in training and he is the extra player in training, if you will," Tuchel added.

Alonso praises Palmer's quality and attitude

Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka misses out on the November fixtures after sustaining a quadriceps injury against Bayern Munich last month.

The Premier League champions believe the 25-year-old will be absent for six weeks after he was substituted early in the Champions League game against Bayern Munich.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is also not selected after picking up an injury against Croatia in October.

The 23-year-old, who made his England debut in the first international break of the season and was described as "the complete package" by Tuchel, is reportedly in contention to return for the Cherries against Ipswich on Sunday.

Manchester United's Marcus Rashford and Newcastle's Tino Livramento, who both pulled out the last squad prior to any matches being played, also miss out with respective hip and knee injuries.

Como's Trevoh Chalobah is another absentee, while Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly and Rico Lewis have also not been selected.

James Garner of Everton and Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White retain their places after being added to England's last squad prior to any fixtures being played, while Arsenal's Ben White and Inter Milan's Djed Spence return for the first time since the summer.

The Arsenal pair of Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa, who both withdrew from the last England party, are fit and selected.

Urukiko Rwisumbuye rwa Gasabo rwategetse ko Tuyishime Israel afungwa burundu nyuma yo guhamywa n’ icyaha cyo kwica se umubyara Munyentwari Vincent, bapfuye umukino wa Rayon Sports.

Ni icyemezo cyafatiwe mu ruhame mu Kagari ka Kabuye, Umurenge wa Jabana mu Karere ka Gasabo ku gicamunsi cyo kuri uyu wa 5 Ugushyingo 2026.

Ubushinjacyaha bwasobanuye ko iki cyaha cyakozwe mu ijoro rya tariki 2 Kanama 2026, ubwo yari iwabo mu rugo, aho yabanaga na se. Bwavuze ko yamuteye icyuma mu ijosi, mu gatuza, mu mutwe, mu mbavu no ku maboko.

Mu rubanza rwabereye mu ruhame i Jabana ku wa 12 Ukwakira 2026, Umushinjacyaha yari yavuze ko Tuyishime na Munyetwari “ batonganye biturutse ku mupira wa Rayon Sports bumvaga kuri radiyo ariko kandi ko uyu musore yari amaze kunywa icyuma cyitwa Gilbeys.”

Raporo y’isuzumamurambo, nk’uko Ubushinjacyaha bwabisobanuye, yagaragaje ko Munyetwari yatewe ibyuma umubiri wose, kandi ko ikintu nyamukuru cyamwishe ari ijosi ryakaswe ariko ntiriveho neza.

Mu ibazwa, Tuyishime yabwiye Ubugenzacyaha ko yishe se abigambiriye bitewe n’amakimbirane bari bafitanye, kuko ngo ubwo yari amaze kunywa inzoga, yibutse ko ntacyo se yamumariye kandi ko yari yanamwise injiji itarize.

Umushinjacyaha yavuze ko Tuyishime yageze mu Bushinjacyaha, yemera ko yishe Munyentwari biturutse ku makimbirane yagiranye na se, kandi ko se ari we wabanje kugerageza kumwica, aramwigaranzura.

Tuyishime yavuze ko Munyentwari atigeze amwitaho nk’umubyeyi kuva acyiga mu mashuri abanza, akamurera nabi, ntamuhe ibyo kurya, bigera aho atandukana na we, ava i Kigali asubira iwabo i Butare.

Uyu musore yavuze ko byageze ubwo yari afite imyaka 17, asubirana na se, yiga mu mashuri yisumbuye ariko ko Munyentwari yatangiye kujya amutoteza, bongera gutandukana.

Tuyishime yasobanuriye urukiko ko muri Gashyantare 2026 yasubiye kwa se, ariko ngo asanga ntacyo yahindutseho kuko yamusubizanyaga umujinya, kandi ko n’igihe yarwaye igifu ntacyo yamufashije.

Yavuze ko tariki ya 2 Kanama, mbere y’uko barya, baganiriye bumva umukino wa Rayon Sports, anenga umunyamakuru wasesenguraga umukino, ngo se aramubwira ati “ Wowe se ibyo urabizi? Wowe se umurusha amashuri?”

Uyu musore yavuze ko iki kiganiro cyabyaye intonganya zikomeye, Munyentwari ajya kunywa inzoga, na we ajya kunywa amacupa abiri ya Gilbeys, nyuma bombi bajya kuryama.

Tuyishime yavuze ko ubwo bari baryamye, yikanze ko umuntu agiye kumurwanya, asanga Munyentwari afite icyuma mu ntoki, bararwana, umusore arusha umubyeyi we imbaraga, amwica uko.

Mu busesenguzi urukiko rwakoze, rwashingiye ku mvugo z’abatangabuhamya bashinje Tuyishime n’ifoto ya se yerekana ko yatewe ibyuma umubiri wose, rusanga adahakana icyo icyaha kuko yacyemeye ubwo yaburanaga.

Urukiko rwasanze kuba Tuyishime yaravuze ko yabikoze yitabara, umwunganizi we akavuga ko intandaro yo gukora icyaha ari ubusembure buturutse ku kuba se yaramwise injiji, ibyo bigaragaza kuvuguruzanya.

Mu mwanzuro, urukiko rwasanze nta busembure bwabayeho, kuko igikorwa cyo gutongana kwa Tuyishime na se kitahise gikurikirwa n’igikorwa cyo kwica.

Rwakomeje ruvuga ko rwasanze nta n’igikorwa cyo kwitabara cyabayeho, rushingiye ku mvugo za Tuyishime, aho yasobanuye ko yagiye muri saloon, akahakura icyuma yateye umubyeyi we.

Urukiko rwasobanuye ko rwafashe uwo mwanzuro rushingiye ku ngingo ya 107 y’itegeko 68 /2018 ryo ku wa 30 Kanama 2018, riteganya ibyaha n’ibihano rusange, iteganya ko uwahamijwe icyaha cyo kwica umuntu biturutse ku bushake, ahanishwa igihano cya burundu.

Urukiko rwasanze icyaha gihama Tuyishime ari icyo kwica umubyeyi we Munyantwali amukase ijosi, akamutera icyuma ku maboko no mu gatuza.

Rwagaragaje ko ruhuje ibiteganywa n’ingingo z’amategeko, igihano akwiriye guhanishwa ari igifungo cya burundu.

A movie style scenario has emerged in DRC’s Haut-Katanga Province where notorious Maï-Maï militiamen stormed the Governor’s office triggering deadly confrontation with police and soldiers guarding the provincial seat of power.

“A police officer was killed and one of the attackers shot dead during clashes this Friday, November 6, in Lubumbashi,” a source on site told local Radio station during a Swahili news bulletin early Friday.

The source added that the casualties also include four soldiers seriously injured and another in critical condition, admitted to the emergency department.

Several attackers were arrested, according to security sources contacted according to the same source.

In a related report, “an individual identified as a Maï-Maï, armed with a machete, allegedly disarmed a police officer after neutralizing him at the gate.”

However, a pro government version report says there has been NO “incursion of armed Maï-Maï men at the governorate.”

“An isolated incident occurred at the entrance to the Haut-Katanga governorate. A single individual attempted to seize the weapon of a police officer on guard duty. Gunshots rang out, and the intruder was neutralized.”

Meanwhile, another witnesses far away from the incursion said, “At 4 hours from Likasi there was a lot of gunfire crackling, we don’t know the reason.”

The Governor’s Office building is currently secured by the FARDC. The situation is reportedly under control, pending investigation.

KIGALI – Seven miners died after water flooded underground tunnels at a mineral extraction site operated by Calliane Mines Ltd in Nyarugenge District, Kigali City, on Thursday, November 5.

The accident occurred in Mageragere Sector, near the Nyabarongo River, where miners were extracting minerals from underground tunnels.

According to accounts from workers at the site, water suddenly entered the tunnels at around 4:00 p.m., catching miners underground. Some managed to escape, while seven failed to make it out.

There were reportedly about 200 people at the mining site when the incident occurred.

The bodies of the seven victims were later retrieved through an operation involving local authorities and security agencies.

The cause of the flooding had not been officially established by Friday. However, miners suspected that excavation activities may have breached an underground water source connected to the nearby Nyabarongo River.

There were also suspicions that the water may have come into contact with electrical installations at the mine, although this had not been independently confirmed.

Nyarugenge District officials visited the site on Friday and informed residents that all seven bodies had been recovered. Arrangements were being made for the burial of the victims.

Calliane Mines Ltd is a Rwanda-based mining company operating a 400-hectare concession in Nyarugenge District, specifically in the Runzenze area of Mageragere Sector. The concession has two active mining sites.

The company extracts three minerals commonly referred to as 3T minerals: cassiterite (tin ore), wolframite (tungsten ore) and coltan (columbite-tantalite).

The company’s owner is Rubazinda Callixte, who has reportedly been held at Mageragere Prison for some time. Further details about his detention were not immediately available.

Authorities had not provided further details about the circumstances of the accident or whether an investigation had been opened.

Conor Coady made 317 of his 503 club appearances in a Wolves shirt

Wolverhampton Wanderers legend Conor Coady has retired from playing at the age of 33.

The former Wolves skipper, who won 10 England caps as a central defender, has been linked with a move into coaching at club level, having already taken up an opening with England Under-21s , external under Lee Carsley on 4 September.

Coady had also been helping out within his first club Liverpool 's Under-21 set-up, prior to his deadline day departure from Wrexham .

It was at Liverpool where it all began for Coady as a promising midfielder in the academy at Kirkby, where his tall, angular build and highly promising form for the reserve team evoked obvious comparisons in some quarters to fellow Liverpudlian Steven Gerrard.

Coady had made just two first-team appearances when he moved on from Anfield, first on loan to Sheffield United in 2013, before signing for Huddersfield Town at the end of that season.

But he enjoyed most of his success at Molineux after being converted into a central defender by then Wolves boss Nuno Espirito Santo.

He also played for Everton , Leicester City, Wrexham and then on loan at Charlton Athletic last season in his 503-game eight-club career.

Coady was first signed for Wolves by Kenny Jackett in 2015 - and played a major part in the club's promotion back to the Premier League in 2018.

He captained the Wolves team who twice finished seventh and also reached the quarter-finals of the Europa League.

In all, he made 317 Wolves appearances, scoring seven of his career tally - for club and country - of 22 goals, before being allowed to leave on loan for Everton in 2022.

He then joined Leicester for a reported £8.5m in July 2023 after Everton opted not to complete a £4.5m deal to turn his season-long loan into a permanent switch.

Coady then moved on for 13 months on the books at Wrexham , which was ended prematurely before his final loan move to The Valley , to join Nathan Jones' Charlton.

But he had not figured this season prior to his official exit from the Racecourse Ground.

Having worked regularly as a pundit for BBC Radio 5 Live to hint at a future media career, Coady has already been linked with the role of assistant head coach at League One side Barnsley.
